svg.title: SN 46.2 Kāya Sutta — The Body
svg.desc: A discourse visualization of SN 46.2: just as the body endures dependent on nutriment, the five hindrances and the seven factors of awakening persist dependent on nutriment. Superficial attention feeds the hindrances; radical attention feeds the awakening factors.

g.text: Just as this body, sustained by nutriment, endures dependent on nutriment,
and does not endure without nutriment ...
endures dependent on nutriment — does not endure without nutriment
So too, the five hindrances are sustained by nutriment, persist dependent on nutriment,
and do not persist without nutriment.
evameva kho, pañca nīvaraṇā āhāraṭṭhitikā, āhāraṁ paṭicca tiṭṭhanti, anāhārā no tiṭṭhanti.
NUTRIMENT FOR THE FIVE HINDRANCES · PAÑCA NĪVARAṆĀ
Frequently attending superficially to the sign of the beautiful
Frequently attending superficially to an aversive mental image
Frequently attending superficially to dissatisfaction (arati) · laziness (tandi)
Frequently attending superficially to the unsettled mind
Frequently attending superficially to things that lead to doubt
what is frequently attended to becomes the nutriment
nourishes the seven factors of awakening
NUTRIMENT FOR THE SEVEN FACTORS OF AWAKENING · SATTA BOJJHAṄGĀ
Frequently applying radical attention to things suitable for mindfulness
Frequently applying radical attention to wholesome and unwholesome (kusalākusalā)
blameworthy and blameless (sāvajjānavajjā) · inferior and superior (hīnapaṇītā)
Frequently applying radical attention to rousing of energy (ārambhadhātu)
Frequently applying radical attention to things suitable for joy
tranquility of body (kāyapassaddhi) · tranquility of mind (cittapassaddhi)
the basis for calming (samathanimitta) · the basis for non-distraction (abyagganimitta)
Frequently applying radical attention to things suitable for equanimity
So too, the seven factors of awakening are sustained by nutriment, persist dependent on nutriment,
and do not persist without nutriment.
evameva kho, ime satta bojjhaṅgā āhāraṭṭhitikā, āhāraṁ paṭicca tiṭṭhanti, anāhārā no tiṭṭhanti.
